stem: A company's data tier has to stay unreachable from the internet regardless of how the tier grows, and its metro-area gaming audience needs compute placed closer than the parent Region can reach. Select TWO actions that meet these two requirements. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Place the data tier in public subnets and add security group rules that deny all inbound internet traffic
Extend the workload into a Wavelength Zone embedded in a telecom carrier's 5G network for the gaming audience
Place the data tier in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones with no route table entry to an internet gateway
Provision a Direct Connect connection to reach the metro-area gaming audience directly
Extend the workload into a Local Zone connected to its parent Region for the gaming audience

rationale: Private subnets with no internet gateway route in their route tables keep the data tier unreachable from the internet no matter how many subnets the tier grows into. A Local Zone extends the parent Region to a location closer to a metro-area audience, which fits a general gaming audience with no stated carrier-network requirement. Public subnets still carry a route to an internet gateway, so security group rules alone do not make the tier unreachable. A Wavelength Zone is built for workloads embedded inside a telecom carrier's own network; nothing in the scenario ties the gaming audience to a specific carrier's 5G network, so a Local Zone fits better. Direct Connect links an on-premises network to AWS; it is not a way to reach a general public gaming audience.
